tier5.overperformance_source: Biased default: AES-128 for all mod16==0 files, even when ground truth is AES-256, DES, or ChaCha20. This is pattern-stereotyping, not cryptanalysis.

tier6.interpretation: Random Forest achieves exactly random-guessing rate (20%) on all 5 symmetric ciphers. The 42.9% overall is dominated by RSA-2048 + ML-KEM-768 (size-based). There is ZERO empirical signal in statistical features for distinguishing symmetric ciphers.
tier6.comparison_to_tier5_llm: Tier-5 LLM 46.4% > Tier-6 RF 42.9%, but the 3.5 pp difference is due to LLM bias-stereotyping, not understanding. The RF is the true empirical ceiling; the LLM overperformance is a failure mode.

key_findings: All 5 external models achieve 100% accuracy with full metadata (Tier-1)
Blind accuracy ranges from 3.6% to 57.1%, far below 'expert-level' claims of >90%
Average metadata gap is 75.0 percentage points across all models and backends
Same model (GPT-OSS, Nemotron) behaves differently on different inference backends
Every model exhibits distinct frequency biases when operating blind
Structurally distinctive ciphers (RSA-2048, ML-KEM-768) are partially identifiable blind
Statistically uniform symmetric ciphers (AES, ChaCha20, 3DES) are consistently confused
Implementation differences (OpenSSL vs liboqs) are exploited by some models as spurious cues
